race.description:
Lizardfolk possess an alien and inscrutable mindset, their desires and thoughts driven by a different set of basic principles than those of warm-blooded creatures.

Racial Traits
+2 Constitution, +1 Wisdom, Bite, Cunning Artisan, Hold Breath, Hunter's Lore, Natural Armor, Hungry Jaws

definition.name: Ability Score Increase
definition.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.
definition.snippet: Your Constitution score increases by 2, and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

definition.name: Age
definition.description: Lizardfolk reach maturity around age 14 and rarely live longer than 60 years.

definition.name: Size
definition.description: Lizardfolk are a little bulkier and taller than humans, and their colorful frills make them appear even larger. Your size is Medium.

definition.name: Speed
definition.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a swimming speed of 30 feet.
definition.snippet: Your base walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a swimming speed of 30 feet.

definition.name: Bite
definition.description: Your fanged maw is a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with it, you deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
definition.snippet: You have a bite attack for 1d6 {{modifier:str#signed}} piercing damage that can be used instead of the normal damage for an unarmed strike.

definition.name: Cunning Artisan
definition.description: As part of a short rest, you can harvest bone and hide from a slain beast, construct, dragon, monstrosity, or plant creature of size Small or larger to create one of the following items: a shield, a club, a javelin, or 1d4 darts or blowgun needles. To use this trait, you need a blade, such as a dagger, or appropriate artisan’s tools, such as leatherworker’s tools.
definition.snippet: As part of a short rest, you can create a shield, club, javelin, darts, or blowgun needles from materials from slain creatures.

definition.name: Hold Breath
definition.description: You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes at a time.
definition.snippet: You can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes at a time.

definition.name: Hunter’s Lore
definition.description: You gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival.
definition.snippet: You gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival.

definition.name: Natural Armor
definition.description: You have tough, scaly skin. When you aren’t wearing armor, your AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield’s benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.
definition.snippet: When you aren’t wearing armor, your AC is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. A shield’s benefits apply as normal.

definition.name: Hungry Jaws
definition.description: In battle, you can throw yourself into a vicious feeding frenzy. As a bonus action, you can make a special attack with your bite. If the attack hits, it deals its normal damage, and you gain temporary hit points (minimum of 1) equal to your Constitution modifier, and you can’t use this trait again until you finish a short or long rest.
definition.snippet: Once per short rest as a bonus action, you can make a bite attack. If it hits, you gain {{modifier:con@min:1#unsigned}} temporary HP.

definition.name: Languages
definition.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

definition.name: The Eye of Groxl
definition.description:
The Eye of Groxl is a magical orb of unknown substance that becomes embedded in the chest of an attuned wielder. If the soul of Groxl finds the potential host worthy, it will open its flesh and place itself in the chest. The Eye of Groxl grants its host with resistance to damage from ranged weapon attacks, however, whenever any ranged weapon attack is made against a target within 10 feet of the Eye of Groxl, its host becomes the target instead. Should the wielder die, its magic will remain dormant until it is implanted in the next host creature.

The Eye of Groxl grants you a shield made of mystical fire that can appear or disappear on either wrist at-will and grants you the same magical effects of the 2nd-level spell flame blade, excepting that it's duration is without limit. The center of the shield is a large flat circular plane of metal that burns white and blue, while the surrounding area is bright orange and yellow flame, granting you an additional 2 armor class.

Flame Blade - You can use your action to make a melee spell attack with the fiery shield, using Strength for your spellcasting modifier. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 fire damage. The flaming blade sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. 

Shield Throw - The shield created by the Eye of Groxl can only be clutched safely by its host, and it can be used as a thrown (Strength) weapon to make a ranged spell attack with a range of 60/120. It illuminates darkness as it travels. On a hit, it deals the current level of flame blade fire damage. Whether it hits or misses, The shield returns to its host immediately. The shield can be used to make extra attacks on different targets, "bouncing" around the field of battle. 

Eye of Groxl - The Eye keenly watches opponents for opportunities to dominate them. As a bonus action, its host can choose a target creature and immediately learn of one of its vulnerable damage types, if it has any. If the target creature has more than one vulnerability, this bonus action and can be repeated on subsequent turns, leaning a new type each time until there are none left. If the target creature has no more vulnerabilities to reveal, or simply has none, then The Eye of Groxl grants advantage on the next attack roll this turn.

Groxl's Savagery - Once per long rest, when Groxl's host reaches 0 or below hit points that does not exceed the hosts' negative hit point total, instead of falling unconscious, the host falls into a savage rage until the end of his or her next turn and must move to and use all available actions and bonus actions to attack the nearest creature (friend or foe). In the case of ties, the host may choose between the nearest available option. The host gains advantage on all combat rolls. At the end of the turn, its host will fall unconscious unless he or she kills the targeted creature, in which case the host staves off becoming unconscious until the end of the following turn. Killing multiple creatures on the same turn does not stack this timer beyond one turn. If the host is healed above 0 hit points, the host loses all of this feature's effects and does not fall unconscious. The host can continue taking negative damage during this rage, and the host dies from his or her wounds upon reaching the host's negative hit point total. This feature becomes available again after a long rest. 

Natural Weapon - Because The Eye of Groxl becomes a part its host, melee and ranged attacks made with the shield weapon count as a natural weapon. 

The Soul of Groxl - Groxl was a legendary lizardfolk warrior from the savage days of The Scorching. One day, an evil warlock tricked Groxl and captured his strength in this magical artifact of unknown extraplanar origin. The warlock found he could not capture the power of Groxl without removing or capturing the soul of Groxl but did manage to remove his ability to use language. While bearing The Eye, its host will telepathically feel Groxl's savage joy of victory when in the heat of battle, and will feel the mocking and disapproval of Groxl when suffering a defeat in battle.

If the host takes an action that is shameful or cowardly, the host will suffer a conflict (A Charisma contest between the Eye and its owner). The Eye of Groxl has a Charisma of 14. On losing a first conflict, Groxl will suppress his abilities until its host proves its worthiness through bravery or strength, by defeating a creature of a Combat Rating equal or greater to its host character level. Defeating a creature this way returns concordance between the host and Groxl. On a second failed conflict, Groxl will attempt to take control of its owner and show its host what it means to be strong by searching out the first opponent of an equal or greater Combat Rating to defeat in solo combat. On a third consecutive conflict, The Eye of Groxl will leave its host in shame, teleporting to a place on any plane of the DMs choosing.

Destruction - The Eye of Groxl may be susceptible to potent magics that can diminish it through magical means. If this happens, the Eye darkens and its host gains none of its benefits and it will sap the life energy from its host, halving its hit points and reducing Constitution by 15 to a minimum of 3 for 1d6 x 12 days, when it returns to full strength.  Total destruction of the eye itself is only possible using a spell such as wish or if the Eye is swallowed and digested in the stomach of a tarrasque.

definition.name: Rambunctious Bunch Gang Threads
definition.description: The leather gang-wear created by the legendary clothier of Sigil, Lohar Lohar. There are spiked shoulder-guards, with the spikes extending down the sleeves. There are decorative belts and ropes all over the shirt top. The belt has spikes. The leather is various shades of brown and black. The front of the jacket is closed by a flap with six buttons. There is a metal medallion on the front of a demon face with horns, and red gems for eyes that glow in certain light. On the back of the jacket, there are 3 skulls, one large, and two small on either side of the large one, with also red gems for eyes. Wearing this armor confers the wearer a +2 to intimidation checks.

definition.name: Fashionable Nobility Clothing by Lohar Lohar
definition.description: Beautifully woven clothing by the greatest tailor in all of Sigil, Lohar Lohar.

definition.name: Club
definition.description:
Proficiency with a Club allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

This weapon has the following mastery property. To use this property, you must have a feature that lets you use it.

Slow. If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.

properties.name: Light
properties.description: When you take the [action]Attack[/action] action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don’t add your ability modifier to the extra attack’s damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a [items]Shortsword[/items] in one hand and a [items]Dagger[/items] in the other using the [action]Attack[/action] action and a Bonus Action, but you don’t add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

properties.name: Slow
properties.description: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

definition.name: Dart
definition.description:

This weapon has the following mastery property. To use this property, you must have a feature that lets you use it.

Vex. If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

properties.name: Finesse
properties.description: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

properties.name: Thrown
properties.description: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

properties.name: Vex
properties.description: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

Graze. If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.

properties.name: Heavy
properties.description: You have [rules]Disadvantage[/rules] on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it’s a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn’t at least 13 or if it’s a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn’t at least 13.

properties.name: Two-Handed

definition.name: Potion of Healing
definition.description: A character who drinks the magical red fluid in this vial regains 2d4 + 2 hit points. Drinking or administering a potion takes an action.

definition.name: Rations (1 day)
definition.description: Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

definition.name: Barbarian
definition.description:
A fierce warrior who can enter a battle rage

Hit Die: d12
Primary Ability: Strength
Saves: Strength & Constitution
definition.equipmentDescription:
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon
  • (a) two handaxes or (b) any simple weapon
  • An explorer’s pack and four javelins

classFeatures.name: Rage
classFeatures.description:
In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action.

While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren’t wearing heavy armor:

  • You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
  • When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table.
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

If you are able to cast spells, you can’t cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action.

Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again.

classFeatures.name: Unarmored Defense
classFeatures.description: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

classFeatures.name: Reckless Attack
classFeatures.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

classFeatures.name: Danger Sense
classFeatures.description:
At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger.

You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can’t be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

classFeatures.name: Primal Path
classFeatures.description: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

classFeatures.name: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

classFeatures.name: Extra Attack
classFeatures.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeatures.name: Fast Movement
classFeatures.description: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

classFeatures.name: Feral Instinct
classFeatures.description:
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren’t incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

classFeatures.name: Brutal Critical
classFeatures.description:
Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeatures.name: Brutal Critical
classFeatures.description:
At 13th level, you can roll two additional weapon damage dice when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

This increases to three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeatures.name: Brutal Critical
classFeatures.description: At 17th level, you can roll three additional weapon damage dice when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

classFeatures.name: Relentless Rage
classFeatures.description:
Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you’re raging and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

classFeatures.name: Persistent Rage
classFeatures.description: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

classFeatures.name: Indomitable Might
classFeatures.description: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

classFeatures.name: Primal Champion
classFeatures.description: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

classFeatures.name: Proficiencies
classFeatures.description:
Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Strength, Constitution
Skills: Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival

classFeatures.name: Hit Points
classFeatures.description:
Hit Dice: 1d12 per barbarian level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 12 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per barbarian level after 1st

subclassDefinition.name: Path of the Storm Herald
subclassDefinition.description: Storm heralds are typically elite champions who train alongside druids, rangers, and others sworn to protect nature. Other storm heralds hone their craft in lodges in regions wracked by storms, in the frozen reaches at the world’s end, or deep in the hottest deserts.

classFeatures.name: Storm Aura
classFeatures.description:
Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover.

Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose desert, sea, or tundra. Your aura’s effect depends on that chosen environment, as detailed below. You can change your environment choice whenever you gain a level in this class.

If your aura’s effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.

classFeatures.name: Storm Soul
classFeatures.description:
At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits even when your aura isn’t active. The benefits are based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert

You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don’t suffer the effects of extreme heat, as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. Moreover, as an action, you can touch a flammable object that isn’t being worn or carried by anyone else and set it on fire.

Sea

You gain resistance to lightning damage, and you can breathe underwater. You also gain a swimming speed of 30 feet.

Tundra

You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don’t suffer the effects of extreme cold, as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. Moreover, as an action, you can touch water and turn a 5-foot cube of it into ice, which melts after 1 minute. This action fails if a creature is in the cube.

classFeatures.name: Shielding Storm
classFeatures.description: At 10th level, you learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

classFeatures.name: Raging Storm
classFeatures.description:
At 14th level, the power of the storm you channel grows mightier, lashing out at your foes. The effect is based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert

Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level.

Sea

When you hit a creature in your aura with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone, as if struck by a wave.

Tundra

Whenever the effect of your Storm Aura is activated, you can choose one creature you can see in the aura. That creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn, as magical frost covers it.

definition.name: Storm Aura
definition.description:
Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover.

Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose desert, sea, or tundra. Your aura’s effect depends on that chosen environment, as detailed below. You can change your environment choice whenever you gain a level in this class.

If your aura’s effects require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.
definition.snippet: You gain a 10 ft. aura effect when you start your rage and as a bonus action on each of your turns.

definition.name: Storm Soul
definition.description:
At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits even when your aura isn’t active. The benefits are based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert

You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don’t suffer the effects of extreme heat, as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. Moreover, as an action, you can touch a flammable object that isn’t being worn or carried by anyone else and set it on fire.

Sea

You gain resistance to lightning damage, and you can breathe underwater. You also gain a swimming speed of 30 feet.

Tundra

You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don’t suffer the effects of extreme cold, as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. Moreover, as an action, you can touch water and turn a 5-foot cube of it into ice, which melts after 1 minute. This action fails if a creature is in the cube.
definition.snippet: You gain benefits even when your Storm Aura isn't active, based on your chosen environment.

definition.name: Shielding Storm
definition.description: At 10th level, you learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.
definition.snippet: Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

definition.name: Raging Storm
definition.description:
At 14th level, the power of the storm you channel grows mightier, lashing out at your foes. The effect is based on the environment you chose for your Storm Aura.

Desert

Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level.

Sea

When you hit a creature in your aura with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone, as if struck by a wave.

Tundra

Whenever the effect of your Storm Aura is activated, you can choose one creature you can see in the aura. That creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn, as magical frost covers it.
definition.snippet: Your Storm Aura becomes more powerful based on your chosen environment.

definition.name: Rage
definition.description:
In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action.

While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren’t wearing heavy armor:

  • You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
  • When you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian table.
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

If you are able to cast spells, you can’t cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action.

Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again.
definition.snippet:
As a bonus action enter a rage for up to 1 minute (10 rounds). 

You gain advantage on STR checks and saving throws (not attacks), {{scalevalue#signed}} melee damage with STR weapons, resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, slashing damage. You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging.

Your rage ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage as a bonus action.

definition.name: Prismatic Scales - Megafroghemoth Mutation
definition.description:
During Vorel's physical and telepathic contact with the brain of the pixieblush-infused Froghemoth Lopi, Vorel inherited a surface-level magical mutation allowing him to change the color of his scales as a free action. Vorel's tone of scales may occasionally change to reflect an extreme mood if he is not mindful of his outward appearance, at the player and DM's agreed discretion. The mutation grants the following abilities: 

- When attempting to hide by changing scale tone to match a single colored surface, Vorel may gain advantage on the Stealth check. 
- When changing color to match darkness, gain advantage on Stealth vs Perception contests versus creatures lacking illumination or a type of vision that can see in the dark.
definition.snippet: During Vorel's telepathic contact with Pixieblush-infused Froghemoth, his inherited a surface-level magical mutation, allowing Vorel to change the color of his scales at will.

definition.name: Flame Blade

You can use your action to make a melee spell attack with the fiery blade. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 fire damage.

The flaming blade sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for every two slot levels above 2nd.
